title: After the Failed Attempt
summary: Lynleit interrogates Kyrien after his failed attempt against an MSF-protected Magus politician nearly harms her, then converts his prison risk into a secret recruitment without telling him she was present.
purpose: Creates the concealed personal tension and coercive bargain that begin Kyrien's hidden association with MSF. Lynleit knows he almost harmed her, while Kyrien cannot account for the personal edge in her questions. She still places the approaching threat and MSF's needs above the injury, using him as an ally Helena cannot anticipate.
known: Kyrien has made a failed attempt to assassinate a politician who belongs to the Magi world.
The politician is under MSF protection when Kyrien makes the attempt.
Lynleit is present and is almost harmed unintentionally during the failed attack.
Lynleit knows Kyrien nearly harmed her, but Kyrien does not know she was present.
Lynleit never tells Kyrien that his attempt placed her in danger.
The immediate aftermath brings him into a police office.
Lynleit conducts the interrogation.
Lynleit invokes an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract, drafted under Fionn for extraordinary threats.
The transfer gives her control of Kyrien's case, and she does not disclose the secret recruitment to Fionn.
Kyrien faces prison unless he agrees to become Lynleit's secret helper.
His freedom remains conditional on accepting Lynleit's demands, leaving him confined to her whims.
Lynleit's private strategy is to keep Kyrien as a secret trump card against Helena.
The recruitment occurs within the first few chapters, well before Fionn's assassination.
Lynleit acts because her intuition warns her of near-future danger before she has enough evidence to define it.
Lynleit is Fionn's biological daughter. Helena is Lynleit's stepmother and Fionn's wife.
Lynleit already suspects Helena of being an enemy despite that family relationship.
Kyrien's father held an important position in Narvea's military.
The targeted politician was involved in causing his father's death.
Kyrien obtained the knowledge and tools for the attempt through his father's military background.
The attempt fails solely because the politician belongs to the Magi world.
The politician's survival later creates consequences for Lynleit.
Lynleit notices Helena probing Fionn's schedules, visitors to the family house, trusted officers, and Lynleit's own travel.
Lynleit suspects murder because Helena appears to be studying the family too carefully.
openQuestions: What is the politician's name, office, and exact role in Kyrien's father's death?
How does the surviving politician later retaliate against Lynleit?
What initial cover story conceals Kyrien's release and unofficial MSF association?
continuityBefore: Kyrien's father's death, the politician's involvement, the MSF protection assignment, and the military knowledge behind the attempt still need connective scenes.
continuityAfter: Kyrien enters Lynleit's service unwillingly without knowing that the handler controlling his case was nearly harmed by his attack. Lynleit must later decide who, if anyone, can be trusted with the recruitment. The arrangement preserves him as hidden leverage against Helena through the early investigation. Fionn's much later assassination vindicates Lynleit's warning without proving that she understood its source.

title: The Secret Third Ally
summary: Lynleit eventually tells only Felix and Reiner that she has recruited Kyrien as an unknown ally and possible trump card against Helena, keeping the decision hidden even from Fionn.
purpose: Defines Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision early in the story, turns secrecy into an advantage over Helena, and establishes the split between Reiner's trust in Lynleit's judgment and Felix's lasting distrust of Kyrien.
known: Helena knows everyone already inside Lynleit's circle, so an unknown ally creates a favorable information imbalance.
Felix and Reiner are already Lynleit's close, long-standing friends before the story begins, not subordinates who become her friends during this crisis.
Lynleit eventually confines Kyrien's recruitment to Felix and Reiner and does not inform even Fionn.
This is Lynleit's first deeply anti-protocol MSF decision, made with strong intuitive conviction.
Fionn's assassination is still far ahead when the compartment is created.
The later assassination validates Lynleit's sense of approaching danger, although it does not prove she foresaw the event itself.
Felix and Reiner both regard Kyrien as a possible threat to Lynleit, especially when neither bodyguard is near her.
Reiner accepts the arrangement because he chooses to trust Lynleit's judgment.
Felix accepts only after Reiner's decision leaves him in the minority.
Felix never fully learns to trust Kyrien and later clashes with him repeatedly.
Lynleit reprimands Felix when those clashes interfere with her decision or the arrangement around Kyrien.
openQuestions: Where and when does Lynleit disclose the compartment to Felix and Reiner?
What evidence or argument does Lynleit use to justify trusting Kyrien?
What continuing cover story protects the compartment from Fionn, Helena, the police, and the wider MSF?
Which clash between Felix and Kyrien produces the most serious consequence for Lynleit or an operation?
What would Fionn do if he learned Lynleit had hidden Kyrien from him?
continuityBefore: Lynleit has already coerced Kyrien into service after the failed assassination attempt, but the arrangement initially exists only between handler and asset.
continuityAfter: Reiner becomes the stabilizing vote that permits the compartment to continue. Felix complies without trust, creating recurring friction with Kyrien and forcing Lynleit to defend the judgment on which the entire imbalance depends.

title: Ash in the Family House
summary: Before the crisis reaches her home directly, Lynleit clumsily chases a grey male cat named Ash, catches him, then cannot bring herself to expel him into the rain.
purpose: Shows Lynleit's clumsy and childish private side while using the grey intruder as an omen. Outside threats and tragedies have begun to bleed into her life, and the escaping cat becomes an emotional symbol for her slipping leads, understanding, and sense of safety.
known: The scene occurs in the early chapters, after danger has begun outside but before Lynleit's life starts to collapse.
The grey cat is male and is named Ash.

known.text: Ash's trespass and permanent stay allow the reader to treat him as an omen of outside threats entering Lynleit's private life without any character naming him as one.

known: The family maintained an original house in Turon while Lynleit's mother was alive and Lynleit was in junior school.
After her mother's death, the family moved to a Vilen residence for Fionn's access to the capital. Lynleit accepted the move only after securing the third-floor study-bedroom.
The Vilen house is a three-floor family residence on a wooded hill above the river that flows toward the city center, with a small rear park and garden.

Lynleit values the thick vegetation and the sound of leaves and branches in the wind. She regards nearby flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning.
The garden-facing first floor contains glass-enclosed relaxation areas that preserve contact with nature through every season.
Lynleit personally chases Ash through the house, revealing a clumsier and more childish side of her than her public role usually permits.

known.text: The chase can imply that Ash's repeated escapes echo Lynleit's fear that her leads, understanding, and safety are also escaping her control.

known: Lynleit eventually catches Ash.
She cannot bring herself to expel him because rain is falling outside.
Ash decides to remain and becomes a permanent loiterer in the family home.
openQuestions: Who else in the household accepts or resists Ash's permanent presence?
continuityBefore: The first disappearances have begun outside Lynleit's private life, but the full crisis, Fionn's death, and the destruction of her family security remain ahead.
continuityAfter: Ash remains inside the house as a quiet domestic echo of the danger Lynleit cannot keep outside. Later losses can turn the once-comic chase into an omen whose meaning becomes clear only in retrospect.

title: The First Missing Man
summary: The first man to disappear appears to be the Spill's first victim, but he independently causes the crisis. His identity and significance remain concealed for most of the story while hidden factions begin exploiting the catastrophe he created.
purpose: Makes the apparent first victim the buried cause of an independent crisis, allowing a later identity revelation to reframe both the Holumn disappearances and the agendas built around them.
known: The first missing person is a man.
He is the person who causes the Spill.
His identity and significance are not revealed for most of the story.
He initially appears to be a victim. His role in causing the crisis remains concealed.
The Spill begins independently of the hidden conspiracy and is later exploited by other actors.
Other factions recognize and exploit the crisis for their own purposes.
The later disappearances are caused by Holumns.
openQuestions: Who is the man?
How does he cause the Spill?
Why does his identity become pivotal later?
Which faction first recognizes and exploits what he caused?
Who notices his disappearance first?
continuityBefore: His public identity and ordinary routine must conceal the significance he will acquire later.
continuityAfter: Holumns begin taking further victims. Investigators treat the first disappearance as the start of the case and do not know that the missing man caused the crisis.

title: The Warning Dismissed
summary: State Councillor Drake becomes convinced that a coup is developing somewhere inside Narvea, but neither his peers nor the Duke believe he has found more than disconnected irregularities.
purpose: Establishes the political explanation that first draws government figures toward the disappearances. Court resentment over Drake's friendship with the Duke deepens his isolation until an illegal alliance feels necessary.
known: Drake is deeply convinced that a coup is underway.
Drake holds the rank of State Councillor and has an unusually close personal relationship with the Duke.
Their friendship begins when Drake is the only official willing to tell the Duke that the Duke is wrong.
The Duke openly refers to Drake as a close friend and sometimes forgives his mistakes.
Courtiers shun Drake as the Duke's pampered favorite and overlook that he originally earned the relationship by refusing to flatter him.
He cannot yet identify where the conspiracy begins or how far it reaches.
His peers ridicule the suspicion and the Duke remains skeptical.
Drake interprets the park disappearances as possible cover for the illegal movement of material intended for action against Narvea or Ducal authority.

known.text: The mismatch between Drake's political evidence and the park's impossible events lets the reader infer that the apparent coup is a mask over a deeper conflict involving Fionn, foreign Magiarchs, and church actors.

openQuestions: What first convinces Drake that the irregularities form a coup attempt?
Which peers lead the ridicule at Court?
Is somebody deliberately encouraging the Court to dismiss him?
Which criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors are shaping the conspiracy from outside Drake's field of view?
continuityBefore: Early disappearances and irregular movements need to produce the evidence that Drake reads as one political pattern.
continuityAfter: Sherie responds to her uncle's isolation by proposing contact with Lynleit outside every lawful chain of supervision.

title: A Meeting Beyond Authority
summary: At night on a hill overlooking Vilen, Sherie leads an illegal negotiation in which Drake seeks limited access to MSF resources without surrendering sensitive evidence.
purpose: Binds the government and MSF investigations together through an alliance that is politically dangerous before anyone understands that the underlying threat is magical. It is Sherie's first independent diplomatic success, not a transfer of Drake's wider role as the story's primary strategic mind.
known: Sherie believes her uncle when the Court does not.
Sherie is Drake's niece and is training under him to become a diplomat.
The approach to Lynleit is entirely Sherie's idea and strategy.
Sherie develops the plan against Drake's wishes, persuades him to participate, and takes charge of the meeting and negotiations.
Drake remains opposed to the illegal approach but attends after Sherie overcomes his resistance.
After the negotiation succeeds, Sherie asks Drake to praise and pamper her for her first achievement.
Drake still cannot decide whether an alliance with Lynleit is a strategic advantage or a dangerous mistake.
Drake remains the story's main strategic mind before and after this event.
The meeting takes place at night on a hill overlooking Vilen.
Drake does not hand sensitive evidence to people outside the aristocratic circle. He and Sherie request access to selected MSF resources and capabilities in exchange for concessions or favors.
Sherie and Drake bring Heyk as their bodyguard and confidant.
Lynleit brings Felix, Reiner, and Kyrien as her bodyguards and confidants.
The main negotiation belongs to Lynleit, Sherie, and a reluctant Drake, while the others contribute opinions and warnings.
Lynleit regards the request as dangerous.
Felix openly protests, while Kyrien stays silent and tests the suspected conspiracy against his own past grievances.
openQuestions: What concessions or favors do Drake and Sherie offer for the confirmed river-surveillance operation?
What access or resources does Lynleit refuse beyond the limited operation?
What would finally convince Drake that the alliance should be preserved or abandoned?
continuityBefore: Sherie must persuade Drake that Lynleit is worth the legal and political danger of contact.
continuityAfter: Sherie claims praise and pampering for her success while Drake remains uncertain about what she has created. The private agreement then produces a narrow intelligence operation. The team may inspect the suspected shipment but cannot arrest anyone or seize material.

title: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge
thread: The suspected coup and the Spill
location: A Vilen river bridge linking a city street to the quarantined park
summary: A covert MSF team descends from a bridge to inspect small night shipments requested by Drake and Sherie. The tarp-covered wooden boats arrive empty, the Drowned Choir attacks from below, and Kyrien secretly witnesses Lynleit burn the drowned hands and stand on the river.
purpose: Carries an operation framed as contraband surveillance into the supernatural without a formal reveal. The failed watches give Lynleit and Kyrien a voluntary card-game ritual before shared danger, then the Drowned Choir turns Lynleit's drowning fear into uncontrolled blue flame and forbidden water walking. Kyrien leaves with a secret he chooses to protect.
known: Sherie and Drake ask Lynleit to assemble a loyal MSF team and investigate recurring night traffic on the Vilen river.
Drake's intelligence identifies small boats moving only on the darkest nights. No operator is visible, the pattern appears intricate, and contraband remains a plausible explanation.
The chosen bridge links a city street to the quarantined park.

The plan requires Felix to freeze the bridge's civil safety cameras, maintain communications, and remain on the city side as fallback while the river team descends by rope, inspects the boats, and leaves by rope at the next bridge.

Several nights produce no boats. Each unsuccessful watch consumes the limited camera window and exposes Lynleit or Kyrien to small oddities emerging from the quarantined park that the mission gives them no freedom to pursue.
After an unsuccessful watch is formally aborted, Lynleit and Kyrien play short card games while the camera feed and bridge equipment are restored.
Kyrien wins the first game through technical play, and Lynleit requests a rematch because she cannot read him.
Across the failed watches, Lynleit learns that Kyrien briefly stops breathing before a risky play. Kyrien learns the small hand movement that precedes one of Lynleit's decisions.

known.text: Their continued rematches and attention to each other's physical tells allow the reader to recognize attraction before either character names or prioritizes it.

known: The successful interception occurs on the fifth watch.
The unsuccessful watches reveal a branch breaking before the wind reaches the trees and a pale interruption in a frozen camera feed.
The boats are small wooden craft with dark tarps over shallow holds. Fixed rudders keep them aligned while the current provides most of their movement.
When the boats finally appear, Reiner, Lynleit, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo descend and find them empty. Felix remains ashore.
The final card game remains unfinished when the boats appear.
When an empty boat shifts, Kyrien briefly steadies Lynleit at the waist near the Sparrow holster above her tailbone. Lynleit allows the contact, and Kyrien releases her before she asks.

known.text: The empty boats, drowned hands, and pale girl imply that the Drowned Choir took the contraband crews before the interception, although the surviving officers cannot prove that connection.

known: The river attack begins while the officers search the empty boats for another explanation.
The officers are capable swimmers. Reaching shore becomes difficult because unseen hands seize their legs and pull downward.
After reaching land, Maren describes the sensation of hands gripping and pulling her legs.
Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the street-facing city bank with Felix's fallback line without understanding what attacked them. They do not realize that Lynleit remains behind.

known.text: The dead hands, the pale girl's drowned voices, and the pattern of new victims imply that she has bound people who drowned in the river across generations and uses them to pull others under.

known: Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly. They seize her most violently and drag her underwater.
Lynleit wears a fitted blue suede jacket for the operation because it interferes less with ropes and wet timber than her usual coat.
The hands tear the blue suede jacket away during the underwater struggle.
The attack activates her childhood fear of drowning. Fury releases her blue flame at unsafe volume, and the fire catches and burns the drowned hands even beneath the water.
After breaking the surface, Lynleit's palm meets resistance. She brings a knee and then both boots onto the same yielding layer until she stands above the river.
The drowned hands reach upward from the darkness but cannot pass through the surface layer beneath Lynleit's feet.
A pale girl emerges wearing a dress made from dead fish. Fishing line sews her eyes shut.

known.text: The girl's silence and tilted head imply that a person standing on water contradicts the rule by which she takes victims.

known: Kyrien is present as Lynleit's concealed unofficial asset rather than an acknowledged MSF officer.
The force in the river separates Kyrien from the official team and drives him toward the quarantined park side of the river.
Kyrien reaches the park bank, enters the trees, and observes Lynleit's confrontation on the river from inside the quarantine.
Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit walking on water.
Lynleit tests each step across the yielding surface and backs toward the park bank while the girl remains still.
Kyrien is too careful to acknowledge what he saw and feigns innocence convincingly.
Lynleit reaches the park side of the river without the jacket, where Kyrien is waiting among the trees.
They remain inside the night park, drenched and struggling to catch their breath.
They sit with their backs pressed together to share body heat while they recover.

The contact makes each of them aware of the other's breathing through their soaked clothes, continuing the physical tell-reading established during the card games without displacing the danger of the river.
Lynleit indirectly asks whether Kyrien saw anything strange during the escape.
Kyrien denies seeing anything, and his careful performance of innocence gives Lynleit nothing she can safely test.

known.text: Kyrien's decision to protect the secret, made without an order from Lynleit, implies the first voluntary trust inside their coerced alliance.

openQuestions: What form does the river's scar take, and in what sense does the place remember the encounter?
What intelligence survives the failed operation beyond the officers' separate accounts?
Does the submerged blue flame leave a lasting injury on the Drowned Choir or only force the hands to release Lynleit?
continuityBefore: The hilltop agreement gives Drake and Sherie access to a small loyal MSF team without granting them control of the agency. Their first request is a limited investigation of apparently unmanned river shipments, with contraband still the leading material explanation.
continuityAfter: Felix, Reiner, Maren, and Ivo carry an account of impossible resistance from the city bank but no shared sight of its cause. Kyrien observes the river from the quarantined trees, and Lynleit later joins him on the park bank without the blue suede jacket. Their back-to-back recovery combines the physical awareness established during the failed watches with a mutual silence around what he witnessed. Lynleit later complains about the lost jacket. Much later, after Fionn's murder, the hotel-room refuge deepens that physical trust into emotional reliance.

title: The Last Man out of the Park
summary: A specially equipped paramilitary unit enters the sealed park and is massacred by forces it cannot understand. Captain Heyk becomes the sole survivor.
purpose: Turns a public missing-person crisis into a state-level containment failure and gives Heyk the grief, access, and personal motive that carry him into Drake and Sherie's service.

characterAnchors.beat: The Last Man out of the Park

known: The park quarantine follows the disappearances of citizens, private investigators, and police officers.
Police enforce the first closure before the park is sealed even from them.
The government deploys specially equipped paramilitary units to investigate the whole park.
The unit commanded by Captain Heyk is massacred by forces he cannot understand or explain.
Heyk is the sole survivor.
The Ducal Guard evacuates him briefly under Drake's orders.
He is subsequently recruited into the Ducal Guard as a field agent and bodyguard serving Drake and Sherie's interests.
His continuing motive is grief for the squad he lost.
openQuestions: What does Heyk perceive during the massacre, and which parts of his account can he articulate?
Why does Drake have enough warning or access to order the Ducal Guard evacuation?
What evidence, equipment, or injury leaves the park with Heyk?
continuityBefore: The public already knows that people are missing. Gas, poison, or another harmful substance remains a possible explanation, although no bodies have been recovered.
continuityAfter: Heyk enters Drake and Sherie's orbit carrying grief, survivor knowledge, and direct experience that no official material explanation can fully contain.

title: Beyond the Cordon
summary: Hiyu enters the quarantined park to test his impossible suspicion that magic is involved in the disappearances. Yulia goes with him to prove the theory wrong and keep him alive.
purpose: Places two opposite investigative methods inside the same impossible case: Hiyu's generative intuition reaches the right category without understanding it, while Yulia's disciplined criminology loses the ordinary rules it depends upon.
known: Hiyu and Yulia are university students in their mid-twenties who study criminology.
Yulia is a classical ISTJ and the top student in their class, with meticulous command of detail and criminological protocol.
Hiyu is an ENTP whose personal investigations rely on intuitive threads, improvised methods, and rapid hypothesis generation.
Without knowing that magic exists, Hiyu suspects it is involved in the disappearances.
Yulia enters partly to prove him wrong and partly to prevent him from facing the danger alone.
openQuestions: How do they bypass the cordon?
What do they find, and how do they survive or escape?
What lasting evidence, injury, or change in their relationship follows the trespass?
continuityBefore: The widening disappearance case gives Hiyu enough fragments to form an impossible but directionally correct theory. Yulia rejects the conclusion but refuses to let him test it alone.
continuityAfter: Their evidence connects two civilian students to the larger institutional response. Hiyu correctly suspects magic but still lacks any complete knowledge of it.

title: Shelter after the Accusation
summary: After exhausting her available resources to escape the directed hunt for her arrest, Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout and finally loses the composure that carried her through the immediate crisis.
purpose: Marks a much later threshold in an intimacy that began functionally after the river incident. Safety, grief, and care turn the coerced alliance into emotional reliance without making the relationship sexual yet.
known: Lynleit acts rationally and efficiently during the accusation and escape.
Helena's response is a directed hunt for Lynleit's arrest.
Lynleit uses every available resource she can reach to evade capture.
Her emotions surface only after she reaches safety in Kyrien's hotel room.
She stays the night.
There is no sexual interaction between them.
Kyrien holds her while she falls asleep.
The hotel-room refuge occurs much later than the river incident and only after Fionn has been murdered.
Their earlier intimate encounters are non-sexual and arise functionally from isolation, danger, cold, near drowning, or emotional rupture.
The first trigger is Kyrien's silent protection of Lynleit's water-walking secret and their back-to-back attempt to share body heat after the river incident.
Lynleit does not pursue attraction as a separate goal. It develops inside work and danger that remain more important to her.
Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of Arc 1.

known.text: The opening of Arc 2 lets the reader infer that Lynleit's disappearance concealed a pregnancy near the boundary between the two arcs.

openQuestions: How does Lynleit locate the hideout without leading pursuit to Kyrien?
What does she say once her composure breaks?
What changes between them the following morning?
continuityBefore: Helena has used Fionn's death to frame Lynleit and direct a hunt for her arrest, forcing her to rely on the secret ally she recruited long before the danger became visible.
continuityAfter: Their bond remains non-sexual at this point, but it becomes a private source of safety within Lynleit's continuing effort to reclaim MSF. Kyrien next helps her establish contact with Felix and Reiner and later chooses to remain after the original bargain has lost its practical force.

title: The First Lines Back into MSF
summary: While Lynleit remains the target of an active arrest hunt, Kyrien helps her find secure ways to contact Felix and Reiner. Their reconnection becomes the first step in her slow campaign to reclaim MSF from Helena.
purpose: Bridges Lynleit's immediate escape and hotel refuge to an organized counteroffensive. The hidden ally Helena did not know becomes the route back to the two trusted officers she does know.
known: Lynleit remains actively hunted for arrest after escaping the immediate accusation.
Kyrien helps her find ways to contact Felix and Reiner without surrendering her location.
Felix and Reiner are the first trusted MSF officers brought back into her fugitive network.
The renewed contact begins Lynleit's slow effort to reclaim MSF from Helena.
Helena's seizure of MSF and the hunt for Lynleit leave the original handler-asset bargain without practical force.
Kyrien has a real opportunity to leave the counteroffensive and chooses to remain beside Lynleit.
The counteroffensive develops while Lynleit remains hunted.
openQuestions: What secure method does Kyrien use to reach Felix and Reiner?
Which officer responds first, and how does Lynleit prove the contact is genuine?
What first foothold inside MSF can Felix and Reiner give her without exposing themselves?
Which arresting authorities and MSF units are actively searching for Lynleit at this point?
continuityBefore: Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel room after exhausting her immediate escape resources. Helena's seizure has also broken the practical authority behind Lynleit's original bargain with Kyrien.
continuityAfter: Kyrien's voluntary decision to remain separates his loyalty from the coercion that began their association. The four-person link gives Lynleit an internal line into Helena's MSF and begins a prolonged contest for legitimacy, intelligence, and control under the pressure of an active manhunt.

title: At the End of the First Arc
summary: After a story-long accumulation of functional trust and non-sexual intimacy, Lynleit and Kyrien finally have sex at the end of Arc 1, shortly before Lynleit disappears.
purpose: Completes a progression that begins with protected knowledge and shared warmth after the river incident, deepens through emotional refuge after Fionn's murder, and becomes sexual only when Arc 1 is closing.
known: Lynleit and Kyrien's intimacy develops slowly and functionally across the entire story.
Short card games during the failed river watches create a voluntary private rhythm before the Drowned Choir attack.
The relationship remains non-sexual through the river aftermath and the much later hotel-room refuge.
Kyrien chooses to remain beside Lynleit after her authority over him can no longer enforce the original bargain.
MSF duty and Lynleit's personal missions remain her priorities throughout the relationship.
Their relationship becomes sexual at the end of Arc 1.

known.text: The opening of Arc 2 lets the reader infer that Lynleit became pregnant near the boundary between the arcs, without a direct explanation or shown realization.

openQuestions: What final circumstances bring them together at the end of the arc?
Is this encounter the conception of their son?
What details at the opening of Arc 2 make the pregnancy inference clear without explaining or showing it directly?
How much time passes between the encounter, the beginning of the pregnancy, and Lynleit's disappearance?
continuityBefore: The failed watches establish voluntary competition and physical attention. The river incident establishes silent trust, the hotel-room refuge establishes emotional safety, and Kyrien's later choice to remain makes his loyalty independent of the original coercion. These changes accumulate inside Lynleit's continuing MSF mission.
continuityAfter: Lynleit disappears near the transition into Arc 2. The opening of Arc 2 supplies enough evidence for the reader to infer the pregnancy, while Kyrien directs MSF without knowing that she carries their son.

title: The Nameless Street
location: Vilen old town and an untraceable street
summary: During a casual walk after lunch with Felix, Lynleit enters a deserted labyrinthine street, follows a crying girl with a red balloon, sees a dead boy below a broken fence, and is pushed from the same ledge before waking on an ordinary city bench.
purpose: Gives Lynleit a private memory of a child's fatal fall that later overwhelms her when she sees Fionn below the hill at the family house. Helena can use Lynleit's genuine shock as emotionally credible evidence for a false accusation.
known: The Nameless Street is an urban myth in the old town of central Vilen.
Under unknown conditions, a lost visitor may enter it alone.
Its buildings and routes form a labyrinth that does not obey the surrounding city.
The warning attached to the myth is not to follow anyone encountered there, because those who do may never return to ordinary streets.
Days before Fionn's murder, Lynleit is walking with Felix after a work lunch when she abruptly finds herself alone, dizzy, unsteady, and suffering a severe headache.
A little girl carrying a red balloon appears, loses it, and runs away crying.
Lynleit catches the balloon by its thread and follows the girl's cries so she can return it.
The girl eventually stands beside a broken fence above an abrupt drop, looking down at the body of a dead boy.
Lynleit releases the balloon in shock. The girl smiles and pushes her from the ledge.
Before reaching the ground, Lynleit wakes on a bench in the ordinary city center while Felix fans her face with a piece of paper after her apparent faint.
Whether the street is a place, an illusion, or another kind of Holumn remains unresolved.
When Lynleit later sees Fionn's body below the hill at the family house, the memory of the boy stupefies her and gives Helena leverage to accuse her of pushing Fionn.

known.text: Because Lynleit perceives no threshold and Felix witnesses only a faint, the reader must infer whether the street is a physical place, an imposed event, or an experience confined to her consciousness.
Felix does not explain why he accepts Lynleit's implausible account without laughing, leaving his response to be read through their long friendship.

openQuestions: What conditions admit a visitor to the Nameless Street, and why does it take Lynleit on this day?
Are the girl and boy inhabitants, repeated roles, former victims, or images produced by the street?
Does the fall release Lynleit, or does another interruption return her to the bench?
Does the street anticipate Fionn's death, draw from Lynleit's future, or leave a pattern that later events happen to reactivate?
What does Felix observe between Lynleit's last ordinary step and her collapse?
continuityBefore: Lynleit is already watching Helena study her family, but Fionn remains alive and the danger has not yet broken into an open accusation.
continuityAfter: Several days later Fionn is found below the hill at the Vilen family house. Lynleit's involuntary recognition of the dead boy gives Helena a true emotional reaction that can be assigned a false cause.

title: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach
placementStatus: Middle-story placement confirmed, exact chapter unresolved
summary: Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has shared forbidden knowledge of magic with outsiders. Kyrien corrects her attempt to limit the breach to himself by revealing that Felix and Reiner also know.
purpose: Turns a private breach into pressure for an institutional answer. Lynleit's promise to handle the witnesses on her own terms becomes an early cause of MSF's later conversion from a purely private intelligence company into a partly Magi enterprise accountable to the Magiarchy and the Church.
known: Father Mikhail is the first authority to learn that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge of magic to outsiders.
Lynleit is unprepared for the discovery and promises to resolve the exposure on her own terms.
Mikhail asks whether Kyrien is the only witness, and Lynleit reassures him.
Kyrien immediately states that Felix and Reiner also know.
Mikhail responds by looking at Lynleit in judgment rather than escalating the confrontation openly.
Lynleit again promises to handle the problem in her own way.
Mikhail leaves her with the warning: 'What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.'
The encounter becomes an early cause of MSF's later transformation into a partly Magi private enterprise reporting to the Magiarchy and the Church.
After Mikhail leaves, Lynleit confronts Kyrien privately for exposing Felix and Reiner.
Kyrien does not apologize or retreat. Lynleit does not use her authority to punish him.

known.text: Their delay in stepping apart lets the reader register unwanted physical awareness inside the argument without turning the institutional conflict into a romantic scene.

known: Kyrien remains to help Lynleit address the breach after the argument.

known.text: Kyrien gives no reason for correcting Lynleit, leaving the reader to infer whether literal honesty, distrust of institutional half-truths, or another motive drives him.
Mikhail does not define his authority. His restraint and final warning imply that the Church may later send him back with powers he is not claiming in this conversation.

openQuestions: Where does the confrontation occur, and what evidence prevents Lynleit from denying the original disclosure?
What action does Lynleit mean by handling the problem in her own way?
What narrow authority would allow Mikhail to be sent back to clean up the breach?
What formal agreement later makes MSF accountable to both the Magiarchy and the Church while preserving its private ownership?
continuityBefore: Lynleit has already allowed Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner to operate with knowledge that ordinary MSF officers and outsiders are forbidden to possess.
continuityAfter: Lynleit must create an institutional place for people she refuses to suppress or surrender. Kyrien's refusal to preserve her convenient half-truth creates personal friction, but he remains involved in solving the exposure. The eventual answer changes MSF's mandate and places part of the private company inside the Magiarchal and Church order.

title: The Coat Fionn Left Behind
placementStatus: Middle of Arc 1 confirmed, exact scene unresolved
summary: Midway through Arc 1, after losing a blue suede jacket in the river and after Fionn's death, Lynleit learns that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears with a garment sewn from material called the hide of leviathan.
purpose: Turns a familiar piece of clothing into evidence of Fionn's concealed care. Its protection is useful but conditional, and its autonomous changes of form keep the inheritance from behaving like a passive suit of armour.
known: Lynleit loses a fitted blue suede jacket during the Drowned Choir attack and later complains about the loss because she liked it.
After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wears.
The discovery occurs in the middle of Arc 1.
The replacement is sewn from material called the hide of leviathan.
The coat can shield its user from minor magically induced damage and phenomena.
Wearing the coat is not enough to activate its protection. Lynleit must cover the threatened part of her body or remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs protection.
The coat chooses its own form. It may appear as a coat, scarf, an imitation of Lynleit's lost blue jacket, or another piece of clothing.
Lynleit cannot command the change, which creates occasional practical and comic problems.
openQuestions: When did Fionn replace the original coat, and how did he do it without Lynleit noticing?
How does Lynleit discover the substitution after his death?
What does hide of leviathan mean, and is it connected to the river phenomenon recorded as HI-004?
What counts as minor magically induced damage, and what limits the coat's protection?
Why does the coat choose forms autonomously, and can it refuse the form Lynleit needs?
continuityBefore: Lynleit loses the blue suede jacket during the river operation. Fionn dies without explaining the protective garment he had placed in her wardrobe.
continuityAfter: The inherited coat becomes part of Lynleit's equipment. Its changing forms can preserve the silhouette of the lost jacket, but its protection remains deliberate rather than automatic.

title: Because There's a Battle to Be Fought
summary: Lynleit asks Kyrien why he continues to help her and risk his life when no reward awaits him. He answers immediately: "Because there's a battle to be fought."
purpose: Makes Kyrien's continued involvement legible without turning it into a declaration of love or loyalty. Lynleit wants to keep him out of needless danger, while Kyrien treats a difficult fight as its own reason to act.
known: Lynleit is bewildered by Kyrien's willingness to keep helping her and entering danger when no reward has been promised.
She does not want to place him in danger without necessity.
Kyrien answers bluntly and without hesitation: "Because there's a battle to be fought."
For Kyrien, the existence of a battle is itself a reason to enter it.
The impulse belongs to the same childish competitive streak that makes him want to win every game.

known.text: Kyrien does not say that he is fighting for Lynleit, leaving the reader to judge how much of his persistence is self-directed and how much attachment has entered a motive he still describes as combat.
His need to prove his worth may be directed toward his own standards, the memory of his father, or both.

openQuestions: Which operation or immediate danger prompts Lynleit to ask the question?
How does Lynleit respond to an answer that removes her from Kyrien's stated reason for staying?
Does Kyrien understand at this point that attachment has become part of the battle he keeps choosing?
continuityBefore: Kyrien has repeatedly accepted danger beside Lynleit, but rescue, coercion, and operational necessity do not fully explain why he keeps returning.
continuityAfter: Lynleit can rely on Kyrien without mistaking his involvement for obedience or romance. His later free choice to remain after her authority fails confirms that the answer was not an excuse.

title: Terrors Inside the Academy
placementStatus: Arc 1 placement and concurrency confirmed, exact chapter sequence unresolved
summary: While Lynleit is dispatched to Cardiff, she answers Natalia's request by sending Kyrien into the Magi Academy as Myka's undercover helper. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally.
purpose: Places Myka's education under genuine supernatural pressure, gives Kyrien a mission inside an institution built around knowledge he does not possess, and makes their first contact the foundation of Myka's later decision to join MSF.
known: Myka encounters terrors inside the Magi Academy.
She relies on Natalia for rescue, advice, and support.
Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka.
Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher during Lynleit's Magi Academy years.
Lynleit cannot intervene personally because the Magiarchy and Church have dispatched her to Cardiff to assist Father Mikhail.
Lynleit sends Kyrien into the Academy as a substitute undercover helper.
Lynleit understates the threat and expects the assignment to help Kyrien understand the Magi world.
Kyrien enters the operation as a non-Magus working inside a Magus institution.
The danger Kyrien and Myka encounter exceeds Lynleit's estimate.
Kyrien relies on conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner to keep Myka safe.
Natalia is forced to intervene personally.
This is Myka's first exposure to Kyrien and MSF.
The experience contributes to Myka's later decision to join MSF after graduation.

known.text: The danger persists inside an institution expected to understand magecraft, implying either concealed knowledge, a failure of classification, or a threat the Academy cannot acknowledge openly.

openQuestions: What terrors does Myka encounter, and why can the Academy not resolve them through its own hierarchy?
What cover, objective, and practical access allow Kyrien to operate inside the Academy?
How does Kyrien communicate with Felix and Reiner without exposing the operation?
Which event forces Natalia to intervene personally?
How are the Academy crisis and the Cardiff venture divided across their parallel chapters?
continuityBefore: Myka already relies on Natalia for ordinary academic advice and personal reassurance. Natalia asks her former favourite student Lynleit for help shortly before Lynleit leaves for Cardiff.
continuityAfter: Surviving the Academy crisis contributes to the knowledge and strength with which Myka later graduates at the top of her class. Her first experience with Kyrien and MSF gives her a personal reason to join the agency later.

title: Father Mikhail's Foreign Venture
placementStatus: Arc 1 placement and concurrency confirmed, chapter sequence unresolved
summary: Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff on special-envoy duty and is drawn into a life-and-death operation against several Magi threats. Lynleit is later sent abroad to assist him, without MSF or its conventional arsenal.
purpose: Gives Mikhail a personal Arc 1 sequence that reveals his past, character, and ability as a Church warrior. His forced cooperation with Lynleit exposes a moral divide whose consequences return to the main story in Narvea.
known: Father Mikhail travels to Cardiff to perform special-envoy duties for the Church.
The assignment develops into a life-and-death ordeal.
Mikhail faces several Magi threats alone before assistance reaches him.
He survives and defeats some of those threats, establishing him as a formidable Church warrior.
The venture reveals more of Mikhail's past, personality, and capabilities.
The Magiarchy and Church later request Lynleit's assistance in Cardiff.
Because Lynleit is abroad, she cannot rely on MSF or its conventional arsenal and must depend on her training as a Magus.
Lynleit and Mikhail continue to cooperate, fulfil their missions, and protect one another.
Their methods of solving the crisis are morally incompatible, and the rift between them grows during the operation.
Consequences from Cardiff later enter the main story in Narvea.

known.text: The Academy crisis unfolds in Narvea during Lynleit's Cardiff dispatch, dividing her responsibilities between a mission she must perform herself and a danger she has delegated to Kyrien.

openQuestions: What special-envoy duty brings Mikhail to Cardiff, and which event turns it into a life-and-death operation?
Which Magi threats does Mikhail face, and what Church techniques let him survive them alone?
What part of Mikhail's past is exposed by the operation?
Which specific method divides Lynleit and Mikhail morally while still requiring them to protect one another?
What consequence follows them from Cardiff into Narvea?
How many Chapters belong to the side story, and where do they alternate with the Academy operation?
continuityBefore: Mikhail already serves as a special envoy and has confronted Lynleit over forbidden knowledge. Natalia asks Lynleit to help Myka shortly before the foreign dispatch removes Lynleit from Narvea.
continuityAfter: Lynleit and Mikhail return from a successful but morally divisive cooperation. The Academy crisis has meanwhile forced Kyrien, Myka, Felix, Reiner, and Natalia into their first shared operation.

title: Myka Enters MSF
summary: After surviving the Academy crisis and graduating at the top of her class, Myka is recruited by MSF as a strong Magus.
purpose: Carries the Academy ordeal into Myka's professional life and gives the smaller MSF a highly trained Magus whose history already connects Natalia, Lynleit, and Kyrien.
known: Myka survives the dangers she encounters inside the Magi Academy.
She graduates at the top of her class.
MSF later recruits her as a strong Magus.

known.text: The current chronology suggests that Myka joins after Lynleit disappears and Kyrien assumes control of MSF, but the exact timing remains unresolved.

openQuestions: Does Kyrien personally recruit Myka after becoming interim director?
Which Academy disciplines make Myka a strong Magus, and what can she not yet do despite graduating first?
How does her earlier undercover contact with Kyrien affect their later working relationship?
What role does Natalia play in deciding whether Myka should join MSF?
continuityBefore: Myka's Academy ordeal forces her to apply knowledge under danger and brings Kyrien into her life as an undercover helper.
continuityAfter: Myka enters the post-Spill agency as a trained Magus while Kyrien directs it without magecraft of his own.

title: The Unresolved Assassination
location: The hillside grounds of the Vilen family house
summary: Fionn is found dead below the hill at the Vilen family house after several incompatible agendas converge without one actor controlling the whole outcome. Helena knowingly opens one part of the path, then uses his death and Lynleit's stunned response to seize MSF and frame her.
purpose: Fionn's death connects the hidden conflict to Helena's visible takeover. The unresolved conspiracy contains several motives, partial knowledge, and accidental cooperation, with no single clean chain of command.
known: Fionn is successfully assassinated.
His body is found below the hill at the Vilen family house, but whether the fall kills him, follows another attack, or is staged remains unresolved.
Lynleit's recent memory of the dead boy on the Nameless Street stupefies her when she sees Fionn below the hill.
Helena assigns a false meaning to Lynleit's genuine shock and accuses her of pushing Fionn.
His death creates the opening Helena uses to take control of MSF.
Helena frames Lynleit for the assassination and directs a hunt for her arrest.
Helena knowingly enables one part of the pressure against Fionn without understanding everything that follows.
No single participant controls the complete assassination outcome.
Several incompatible agendas accidentally cooperate to produce Fionn's death.
The broader conflict already includes pressure from criminal Magi, foreign Magiarchates, and church actors.
The unresolved issue is how each participant's intended outcome and partial action converge into the assassination.
openQuestions: What outcome do the criminal Magi seek around Fionn?
What separate outcome does a rival foreign Magiarchate seek?
What separate outcome does a church faction seek?
Which actions accidentally cooperate even though their authors do not share one objective?
Did one faction covertly or illegally infiltrate another and use its people or resources without authorization?
Does any participant's apparent affiliation conceal who truly directed them?
Which door does Helena knowingly open, what does she expect to happen, and what follows beyond her knowledge?
Does the fall kill Fionn, conceal another cause of death, or stage the physical evidence used against Lynleit?
continuityBefore: Manufactured political strife isolates Fionn and divides his attention while the Spill develops. Days earlier, the Nameless Street gives Lynleit an unexplained memory of a boy lying dead below a fall.
continuityAfter: Helena converts the vacancy into control of MSF, makes Lynleit the official suspect, and directs a hunt for her arrest while the true authorship remains hidden.
